alternatives.reason_rejected: Resolves relative to the bundle, which has no sibling JSON; the plugin would silently ship the proven table. Would also need a postbuild copy step that tsc gives for free.

alternatives.option: Generate a TS module from the JSON at build time
alternatives.reason_rejected: Verified unnecessary — both tsc and esbuild handle the JSON import natively; a generated module adds a build step and a second source of truth.

assumptions: The committed src/retrieval/calibration.json is the genuine output of scripts/calibrate-tokenizer.mjs against a real ANTHROPIC_API_KEY — its numbers were not re-derived here, only validated for shape and range
A measured table still warrants conservative_fallback: true, because it is an empirical bound over a named corpus rather than a count
Breaking the packet token_usage shape (new table_provenance field) is acceptable on the v3 line, per the settled 'breaking behaviour is permitted on v3' decision
constraints: Could not run npm run build or touch plugin/ — verified dist and bundle carriage with a scratch outDir and an in-memory esbuild instead
No network: the measured ratios could not be re-verified against the count-tokens API
context: Wired src/retrieval/calibration.json into the tokenizer: ACTIVE_TABLE (measured, validated at load, proven fallback) is now the default for every estimate, packet and briefing. 2711 pass.
rationale: Verified empirically before choosing: tsc emits the file to dist/retrieval/calibration.json (so package.json's existing "dist" files entry already ships it) and esbuild inlines it into the plugin bundle as a plain object literal with no runtime path left behind. createRequire would have resolved relative to plugin/server/twining-server.mjs, where no calibration.json sits, so every plugin user would have silently fallen back to the ~4x-looser proven table — the exact failure mode the wiring exists to close. The cost of the static import is that an absent file is a BUILD error rather than a runtime fallback; that is the safer failure (loud, at build time, versus a silent 4x budget regression in the field), and the absent path stays testable because loadCalibrationTable(raw) is exported and tested with undefined/null/garbage.
summary: Loaded calibration.json with a STATIC import (`with { type: "json" }` + tsconfig resolveJsonModule) rather than createRequire, and kept validation at module load anyway
